change.title: pr-33832-flat
change.description: Add AuthzClientCryptoProvider for authorization client cryptographic operations
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Two providers with the same order no longer fail; one is picked silently by classpath order
findings.body:
The old `foundProviders.size() > 1` check threw `IllegalStateException`, so a deployment that shipped two real providers failed fast. Now every real provider returns 200: `DefaultCryptoProvider` (crypto/default/.../DefaultCryptoProvider.java:83), `FIPS1402Provider` (crypto/fips1402/.../FIPS1402Provider.java:114) and `WildFlyElytronProvider` (crypto/elytron/.../WildFlyElytronProvider.java:76). The sort is stable, so when two of them tie, whichever ServiceLoader returns first wins. That is classpath order, and the losers are only logged at debug level (line 69).

Example: a FIPS deployment that accidentally also has keycloak-crypto-default on the classpath used to refuse to start. Now it may quietly run on the non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider, and nothing at the default log level says so.

Fix: keep the order-based preference, but still throw (as before) when more than one provider shares the highest `order()`. The authz-client provider (order 100) can still lose to a single real provider without an error.

findings.title: Round-trip test only checks the new codec against itself, on one curve for all three algorithms
Dead encoder calls
findings.body: Lines 114-115 build two `ASN1Encoder` instances and throw away the results. The real encoding is done at lines 117-121. These two lines can be removed.

findings.title: New abstract `order()` breaks external CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `CryptoProvider` is a public SPI loaded through ServiceLoader. Adding an abstract method means any implementation outside this repository stops compiling, or throws `AbstractMethodError` at line 57 when sorted. All in-repo implementations were updated. Should this be a `default` method instead, with a documented default value, so third-party providers keep working?

contracts.action: AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now initializes CryptoIntegration with the authz-client classloader
contracts.equivalent_path: CryptoIntegration.init is idempotent: it detects a provider only when none is set yet
contracts.before_after: create() and create(InputStream) both go through create(Configuration), so every factory path initializes. If something else already initialized (e.g. the server), init does nothing.
contracts.visible_effect: ECDSA client-JWT signing (ECDSASignatureSignerContext -> ECDSAAlgorithm.asn1derToConcatenatedRS -> CryptoIntegration.getProvider()) now works in a standalone authz-client instead of throwing 'Please init first'
contracts.failure_mode: If no provider is found, detectProvider throws IllegalStateException from create(). With the authz-client service file always present that can't happen. If providers tie at the top order, one is picked silently (see finding).

contracts.action: AuthzClientCryptoProvider ECDSA DER <-> concatenated R||S conversion
contracts.before_after: Same algorithm as the BC version: pad r/s with a leading zero byte, encode as INTEGERs in a SEQUENCE, and decode back with fixed-width integerToBytes (same truncate/pad logic as X9IntegerConverter).
contracts.visible_effect: The JWS signature of a client assertion sent to Keycloak
contracts.failure_mode: Malformed DER makes IOException propagate from sign(). Indefinite-length DER gives an empty sequence, which is rejected by the size!=2 check.

contracts.action: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider picks the provider with the highest order() instead of failing on multiple providers
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous behaviour: throw IllegalStateException when more than one provider is found
contracts.before_after: Before: more than one provider was an error. After: sort by order descending, take the first, and log the rest at debug.
contracts.visible_effect: Which crypto provider (FIPS/default/elytron) the server or adapter uses
contracts.failure_mode: Default, FIPS and Elytron all return 200, so a tie is broken by ServiceLoader classpath order with no warning.

summary: The PR adds a minimal CryptoProvider to authz-client, so ECDSA client-JWT signing works without BouncyCastle. Its DER codec matches the existing BouncyCastle implementation (BCECDSACryptoProvider). The main problem is in CryptoIntegration. It used to throw when several providers were on the classpath; now it picks the one with the highest order(). Default, FIPS and Elytron all return 200, though, so if two of them are present, one is chosen silently by classpath order. A FIPS deployment that also carries keycloak-crypto-default could end up on the non-FIPS provider without any error. The ECDSA test only checks the new codec against itself, using one default-size key for all three algorithms. There are also two dead lines in the encoder, and a question about adding abstract order() to a public SPI.
